messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya@larksystems.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:15:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed long gaps in streaming chat responses

Hi Sean / Monica,

We're seeing repeated >2s gaps between token chunks in our live chat flows since ~08:40 PST this morning. The UI shows intermittent stalls mid-response: tokens arrive quickly for a few hundred ms, then a silent pause, then rest of response. This happens across multiple regions for our user base.

Attached is a short client trace (client_trace_20261128.txt) showing two samples where chunk delivery pauses for 1.8s and 2.4s respectively. We're on the hosted streaming endpoint via your JS SDK (v0.9.3).

This is impacting user experience — can you confirm if there's a service-side incident and any immediate mitigations we should apply on our side?

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: Observed long gaps in streaming chat responses

Hi Priya — thanks for the trace and flagging this early. We're looking into it right now. Quick notes / immediate steps you can take that may reduce user-visible stalls while we triage: 

- Client retry/backoff: if you see a silent gap >750ms, issue a lightweight range request to the streaming endpoint to resume (our SDK has a streaming_resume helper in v0.9.4; for a short term you can poll the non-streaming chat endpoint every 500ms as a fallback).
- Reduce client-side chunk threshold: set max_tokens_per_chunk=64 (default 128) in the SDK to make tokens appear more frequently during bursts.
- Lower client buffer window: set stream_buffer_ms=150 to flush partial frames sooner.
- Avoid aggressive client-side parallelism: cap concurrent streams to 2 per user during this window.

I've routed logs to Priyom for kernel/runtime triage. We'll follow up with a more detailed mitigation if this looks systemic.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:30:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed long gaps in streaming chat responses

Folks — quick triage notes after looking at edge telemetry: 

- Symptom: increased 'emit latency' on a small subset of streaming shards in us-west-2; tokenization and kernel scheduling fell back to a less-optimal execution path under a rare combination of sequence-length variance + model kv cache thrashing.
- Scope: ~4% of streaming requests served by three edge shards for ~90 minutes starting 08:35 PST on 2026-11-28. The rest of traffic used normal kernel paths.
- Immediate mitigation performed: we rotated the affected shards (rolling restart) at 09:20 and applied a temporary kernel-selection override to prefer the low-latency execution path for chat models with average prefix <512 tokens.

Attached is an edge snapshot we pulled during the window. We'll continue to monitor, but that rotation should have reduced the pause incidence.

Next steps being scheduled:
- We will push a permanent kernel selection adjustment and add a guard for kv-cache churn detection.
- Postmortem with root cause and timeline in 48–72 hours.

P
Priyom Das
Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Interim customer guidance — reduced stalls for streaming chat

Hi Priya — following Priyom's triage, here is a short, copy/paste playbook you can use in your engineering channel or rollback runbook. These are customer-safe, reversible client-side/usage changes that should give you immediate relief while we validate the permanent fix: 

1) Client SDK knobs (recommended order):
   - set max_tokens_per_chunk=64
   - set stream_buffer_ms=150
   - set streaming_timeout_ms=3500 (gives the SDK a short grace before fallback)
   - cap concurrent_streams_per_user=2

2) Gradual rollout suggestion:
   - start with 5% of traffic (canary) for 30m, verify median token-gap drops below 200ms, then 25% for 30m, then full rollout.

3) Fallback strategy if a stream stalls >1500ms:
   - SDK should attempt one quick reconnect (backoff 300ms) and then fall back to the standard non-streaming completion endpoint for that request.

4) Monitoring:
   - track token-gap (time between first and second chunk) and token-gap-95p; alert if 95p > 1000ms.

5) Server-side note for your SRE:
   - our side has rotated the implicated shards and applied a temporary kernel-selection override; we are rolling a permanent kernel-selection patch that prevents the fallback path on small-prefix chats.

I'll paste the same guidance into the support ticket and include the status link: https://status.redwood-inference.example/incidents/20261128-elongated-chunks 

Please reply if you'd like us to push a client-config toggle from our SDK team for you (we can flip max_tokens_per_chunk for your org via a feature flag temporarily).

Sean

Thanks Sean / Priyom / Monica — we implemented the client-side changes as a 10% canary yesterday afternoon and saw the token-gap-95p drop from ~1.6s to ~220ms. After ramping to 50% this morning, the UI stalls are effectively gone for our test cohort.

We're happy with the temporary mitigations. We'd like the full postmortem and the permanent fix ETA so we can decide whether to keep the client-side changes long-term or revert to prior defaults. Can you include the following in the postmortem:

- timeline of the kernel-selection fallback and shard rotation action
- any guidance on whether we should retain max_tokens_per_chunk=64 permanently for chat-heavy flows
- confirmation that this won’t impact latency for long-sequence (document assistant) workloads

If helpful, I'm happy to join a 30-minute sync this week to go over details.
